- [LDET.3.4.4] **Every transcendental is correctly rounded.** Bit-identity
  ([LDET.3.4.1]) extends to the transcendental functions ([LEXP.3.9]), to `**`
  at every exponent ([LEXP.7.3a]), and to the unit conversions, `unit formula`s
  and complex operations built on them ([LUNI.4.3], [LUNI.4.5], [LUNI.14.5]),
  because each is correctly rounded ([LEXP.3.9.2]) and fixed at its special
  values ([LEXP.3.9.3]). Nothing in a compiled bundle reaches a
  platform-variable operation, so there is no envelope to calibrate and no
  result to compare within a tolerance.

  A composite is evaluated as its formula is written, one rounded operation at a
  time ([LDET.3.6.1]). It is not correctly rounded itself, and it is identical on
  every conforming engine. The angle conversions ([LEXP.3.6.1]) and
  `distance.great_circle` ([LEXP.5.11.2]) are composites of this kind.
